CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports right elbow pain that started approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He was throwing a ball when the pain began. His 13-year-old son was "checking" him multiple times with a lacrosse stick during play and may have struck him in the elbow area. Patient denies falling. Pain is sharp in character and occurs with any movement of the elbow. Pain radiates down the forearm. He tried Advil for a couple of days with some relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain and abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus
Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has two children ages 13 and 10. Plays lacrosse with his children. Family follows Mediterranean diet with low salt intake. Had some dietary indiscretion during the pandemic but has been compliant with healthy eating since.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure: 150/90 mmHg
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur present
Right elbow: Pain to palpation of olecranon area of posterior elbow, mild pain with flexion and extension, normal range of motion, visible swelling and bruising

RESULTS
Right elbow x-ray: Normal, no fracture or bony abnormality
Blood glucose levels when patient checks: 80-100 mg/dL
A1C: Ordered

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right elbow contusion secondary to lacrosse stick trauma. Prescribed ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain and swelling. Apply ice three times daily for 20 minutes per session. Avoid playing lacrosse for next couple of weeks to allow healing. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily for hypertension; blood pressure elevated today possibly due to white coat syndrome. Continue metformin 500 mg daily for diabetes management. Will check A1C to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment needed.
